text.en: Believing different isotopes of the same element could in principle be separated using ordinary chemical reactions or filtration, the same way different chemical compounds are separated -- isotopes of the same element have essentially identical chemical properties, since chemistry is governed almost entirely by the number and arrangement of electrons (determined by the number of protons), which is the same for every isotope of a given element; ordinary chemical separation methods therefore cannot distinguish isotopes at all, and every practical isotope separation technique must instead exploit the small difference in nuclear mass between isotopes.
text.et: Arvamus, et sama elemendi erinevaid isotoope saaks põhimõtteliselt eraldada tavaliste keemiliste reaktsioonide või filtreerimisega, samamoodi nagu erinevaid keemilisi ühendeid eraldatakse -- sama elemendi isotoopidel on sisuliselt identsed keemilised omadused, kuna keemiat juhib peaaegu täielikult elektronide arv ja paigutus (mille määrab prootonite arv), mis on sama antud elemendi iga isotoobi jaoks; tavalised keemilised eraldusmeetodid ei suuda seetõttu isotoope üldse eristada, ning iga praktiline isotoopide eraldamise tehnika peab selle asemel ära kasutama isotoopide vahelist väikest tuumamassi erinevust.
